'''Laszlo Milhaly''' is a Hungarian-American [[physicist]]. A member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], he is a [[distinguished professor]] in the department of [[physics]] and [[astronomy]] at [[Stony Brook University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/physics/people/_profiles/mihalyl|title=Laszlo Milhaly|work=[[Stony Brook University]]|access-date=May 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/faculty-pathways/_archive-fp/awards/distinguished.php|title=Distinguished Professorships|work=[[Stony Brook University]]|access-date=May 25, 2026}}</ref>

In 2005, Milhaly was named a [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]], "for important contributions in tunneling and optical studies of high temperature superconductors and fullerene materials, and for developing far infrared spectroscopic methods to detect electron spin resonance".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/winners?q=milhaly&af=false|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=May 25, 2026}}</ref>
